before: Different gene mutations cause different levels of enzyme deficiency, and acute hemolysis is triggered by oxidative stressors including fava beans [1].

Familial Mediterranean fever is a monogenic autoinflammatory disorder caused by mutations in the MEFV gene, mainly affecting people of Mediterranean descent with higher incidence in Turkish, Jewish, Arabic, and Armenian populations [2].

Hemoglobinopathies are the most common single-gene disorders in humans, with 951 of 1,424 described variants involving the β-globin gene, and African, Asian, and Mediterranean populations among the most affected [3].

Familial Mediterranean Fever and MEFV Variants

Familial Mediterranean fever is a monogenic autoinflammatory disorder caused by mutations in the MEFV gene, mainly affecting people of Mediterranean descent with higher incidence in Turkish, Jewish, Arabic, and Armenian populations [7].

Hemoglobinopathies are the most common single-gene disorders in humans, with 951 of 1,424 described variants involving the β-globin gene, and African, Asian, and Mediterranean populations among the most affected [8].
